newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt up in thin trade as players await FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt up in thin trade as players await FOMC.

text.p: Brady bond prices were higher on Friday in followthrough buying from New York but market analysts said trading remained thin ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday.
"Not a great deal is happening. It is slightly firmer with a little followthrough buying from strength in the long bond that we saw late yesterday," an emerging market trader said.

Brazilian Bradys were the biggest gainers as the debt recouped some losses suffered earlier in the week as concerns about an alledged pay-for-vote scheme reported in a local newspaper earlier in the week receded.

Folha de Sao Paulo published on Tuesday what it said were transcripts of secretly taped conversations that revealed five congressmen may have taken bribes to vote for a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term.
It also reported on Wednesday that Brazil's Communications Minister Sergio Motta may have supplied some of the money. Motta denied involvement in the alledged scheme.

"The government has managed to contain any of the fallout from the scandal that has been alleged in one of the local newspapers. It looks as though the market is more relaxed about it and it looks as though the stability of the government is not in any way threatened," said an emerging market analyst.

Brazilian "C" bonds were 3/4 firmer at 76-3/4 bid and the discount bonds were 3/8 stronger at 80-7/8 bid. Analysts said the rise in Brazilian Brady prices also helped bolster other Latin debt instruments.
Mexican par bonds were 5/8 higher at 74-3/4 bid, Argentine FRBs were 1/4 stronger at 92-5/8 and Venezuelan DCBs were 1/8 firmer at 90 bid.
Market sources said trading remained thin ahead of the U.S. FOMC meeting because of continued uncertainty about whether the Federal Reserve will tighten U.S. monetary policy.
"We will see range trading ahead of the FOMC but I think we might see slightly firmer sentiment for the remainder of the day," another market source said.
Among Eastern European debt instruments, Bulgarian IABs were 1/4 higher at 66-1/2 bid and Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans were 1/4 stronger at 84-3/4 bid.
